course_name_original: Máquinas e instalaciones de calor y frío (248301)
course_name_en: Heat and Cold Machines and Installations

learning_outcomes.text: That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects implying knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
That students can transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.

Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering in the specific Mechanical technology, whose purpose is the construction, renovation, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to manage the activities subject to the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering in Mechanical technology.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Possess applied knowledge of thermal engineering.
Possess applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Ability to handle, use, and maintain thermal and fluid equipment and systems.
Ability to measure and analyze data of thermal and fluid variables in machines and systems.
Express and communicate ideas and systems related to thermal energy transmission and refrigeration systems.
Acquire knowledge and skills for the calculation, use, and maintenance of thermal and fluid machines and installations.
Understand and prepare professional technical documentation on energy and refrigeration technology topics.
Master calculations and estimation and design procedures in heat and cold production matters, both in domestic and industrial settings.

syllabus_topics: Calculation of thermal loads and psychrometric chart

assessment_methods.method: Project work and oral presentation of a refrigeration or air conditioning project
Exam, including theoretical and practical aspects with calculations

assessment_rules: If the exam in continuous assessment does not reach the minimum grade of 4.5, the final grade for the course will be a maximum of 4.9 out of 10 (fail), without prejudice to the student's right to take the recovery evaluation. During the recovery period, a single written exam will be held, which will replace both the project work and the ordinary exam, representing 100% of the grade. A minimum grade of 4.5/10 is required for the exam to be weighted in the final grade.
